<div class="diatribe-meta">Book III · 2 paragraphs · <span class="canonical" title="Canonical reference">III 11</span></div>

<nav class="chapter-nav"><a href="3-10.html">Previous discourse</a><a class="chapter-home" href="../index.html">Home</a><a href="3-12.html">Next discourse</a></nav>

<div class="paragraph-list">
<p>THERE are certain penalties fixed as by law for those who disobey the divine administration.<a class="note-ref" id="noteref-1" href="#note-1" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="note 1"><sup>1</sup></a> Whoever thinks any other thing to be good except those things which depend on the will, let him envy, let him desire, let him flatter, let him be perturbed: whoever considers any thing else to be evil, let him grieve, let him lament, let him weep, let him be unhappy. And yet, though so severely punished, we cannot desist.</p>
<p>Remember what the poet<a class="note-ref" id="noteref-2" href="#note-2" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="note 2"><sup>2</sup></a> says about the stranger: <span class="verse-quote"><span class="l">Stranger, I must not, e’en if a worse man come.</span> </span> This then may be applied even to a father: I must not, even if a worse man than you should come, treat a father unworthily; for all are from paternal Zeus. And (let the same be said) of a brother, for all are from the Zeus who presides over kindred. And so in the other relations of life we shall find Zeus to be an inspector.</p>
</div>

<section class="notes">
<h2>Notes</h2>
<ol class="note-list">
<li class="note" id="note-1" role="doc-endnote"><p>As to the divine law, see iii. 24. 32, and Xenophon’s <cite>Memorabilia, iv. 4. 21,</cite> etc. Upton.</p><a class="note-back" href="#noteref-1" aria-label="back to the text">&#8617;</a></li>
<li class="note" id="note-2" role="doc-endnote"><p>The poet is Homer. The complete passage is in the Odyssey, xiv. V. 55, etc. <span class="verse-quote"><span class="lg"> <span class="l">Stranger, I must not, e’en if a worse man come,</span> <span class="l">Ill treat a stranger, for all come from Zeus,</span> <span class="l">Strangers and poor.</span> </span></span></p><a class="note-back" href="#noteref-2" aria-label="back to the text">&#8617;</a></li>
</ol>
</section>
